gaps.sentence: The wedding guests ___ when the string quartet began to play.
gaps.hint: in progress when the music began
gaps.explanation: An action in progress when a past event occurred takes the past continuous: were still arriving.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her laptop repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Has had it repaired twice this year' — present perfect of causative have.

gaps.sentence: When I got to the office, I realised I ___ my security pass.
gaps.hint: the forgetting happened before realising it
gaps.explanation: The forgetting happened before the past moment of realising, so the past perfect is needed: had forgotten.

gaps.sentence: When I was a boy, films ___ in black and white.
gaps.hint: a past state no longer existing
gaps.explanation: 'Used to be' describes a past state that has ended: used to be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ coffee at all, but I drink tea every morning.
gaps.hint: a general habit contrasted with another habit
gaps.explanation: A permanent habit takes the present simple, so the negative form is: don't drink.

gaps.sentence: The conference ___ on Monday and ends on Wednesday.
gaps.explanation: Fixed schedules are stated in the present simple: starts.

gaps.sentence: By the age of thirty, she ___ her own company.
gaps.hint: by the age of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An achievement completed before a past reference point takes the past perfect: had started.

gaps.sentence: Listen! Someone ___ the violin in the flat above us.
gaps.hint: Listen signals an action happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Listen!' points to an action in progress at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous is used: is playing.
